result.reason: The operative language substantially reaches the preferred position: Contractor defends and indemnifies Company and its affiliates against third-party claims involving IP infringement, breach of law, Contractor-caused unauthorized access or disclosure, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with standard notice, defense-control, settlement-consent, and cooperation procedures. It also removes these obligations from the general liability cap; no Customer indemnity is added, which is no broader than the permitted Customer indemnity. However, the draft unnecessarily relocates the existing IP warranty, retains confusing duplicate subsection numbering, and refers to nonexistent Section 7(b). The data-breach trigger is also framed more narrowly as unauthorized access to or disclosure of Company Confidential Information, rather than data breaches generally. These issues make the revision less than minimal and reduce drafting quality, although they do not prevent substantial compliance with the rule.
